parts.title: Growth Strategies for Startups - Initial Tactics and Their Implementation

sentences: In the book "100 Days of Growth," the authors discuss various marketing strategies to help startups grow.
They highlight tactics like giving away **free company t-shirts** to enhance brand awareness and customer loyalty.
Another strategy is sending a **personalized welcome email** to new customers, offering a friendly digital "hi," much like a mom-and-pop shop's welcome.
The authors also suggest the **VIP Beta Launch**, enticing prospects with exclusive access, and using **Help A Reporter Out (HARO)** for free publicity.

Crafting an **education-focused email series** demonstrates your willingness to help potential customers and communicate value through a **promise-oriented headline** on your site, catching visitors' interest in mere seconds.
**Blog regularly** for **business credibility**.
Use **Weekly Roundup posts** to build your reputation by sharing industry content and prove you have the right ideas and solutions.
**Curate and share** quality posts from others to **boost your standing** in your sector.
The **Inactive Users Email** strategy is useful for getting users who signed up for your service but forgot about it to interact with your product again.
Many **SaaS or app companies** face the issue of **inactive users**, and a direct way to engage them is through **engagement-driven emails**.
These emails serve to remind users of your service and motivate them to come back, thus potentially increasing **app usage** and **customer retention**.
To implement this, you need to **track user behavior** and use tools that allow you to **send automated emails** to inactive users.
First, **sign up for an automation tool** to help manage these emails.
Consider what kind of **messages** would re-engage users, and set up email campaigns that automatically trigger based on user inactivity.
Doing this can help in **reactivating forgotten users** who might become valuable customers again.
**User-generated content** is a great way to boost **engagement** and **reach** new audiences, especially on **social media** like Facebook and Twitter.
This strategy involves **content produced** by your **followers**, which also helps **illustrate brand loyalty**.
Some companies run these campaigns for **three main reasons**: strengthening **brand reputation**, leveraging **user experiences**, and requiring **minimal ongoing management** after setup.
To implement a **User-Generated Content (UGC) campaign**, start by deciding on a **concept** that focuses on your products and target **customers**.
Look at **successful examples** like **Warby Parker** or **Starbucks** for inspiration.
Once planned, spread the **word** about your campaign and encourage **loyal customers** to participate, which will help stimulate the campaign's **momentum**.
## The Win-Back Email
The **Win-Back Email** is a strategy to re-engage former customers who have stopped buying from you.
**Smart business owners** see the value in connecting with these past customers, realizing it's often easier to sell to people familiar with their brand.
**Win-Back Emails** showcase new features, offer special deals, and include strong **CTAs** to persuade them to return.
**Step 1:** Identify past customers who left 60-120 days ago.
**Step 2:** Craft a **persuasive email** emphasizing new features and offers.
**Step 3:** Send the email, analyze results, and adjust as needed.
**Tools** like VERO and Customer.io can automate the process, helping you win back these valuable contacts.
